title: The ground didn’t open first.
paragraphs:
“We are all holy… why do you exalt yourselves?” (Numbers 16:3).
That’s what Korah said.
And if you read it too fast, it almost sounds right.
Something that still lives in us.
Because rebellion rarely begins with shouting.

Why them?
Why not me?
Why does God use them like that?
And suddenly, calling feels like competition.
And here’s the part we don’t say out loud…

You can be in the presence of God
and still secretly resist His order.
This is not just an Old Testament story.
Have you ever obeyed God… but resented someone else’s favor?
Have you ever served faithfully… but quietly questioned why your life feels unseen?
Have you ever smiled publicly… but wrestled privately with jealousy?
The Bible says, “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall” (Proverbs 16:18).
Korah didn’t fall because the ground opened.
The ground opened because he already fell.
God didn’t create the crack—He revealed it.
And here’s the spiritual mirror most people avoid:
You don’t have to leave God to rebel against Him.
You just have to stop trusting His placement.
You just have to start believing you deserve more than what He assigned.
And suddenly, your heart is negotiating with God.

Delayed obedience.
Selective surrender.
Silent resistance.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Some people don’t walk away from God…
He questioned God’s authority behind Moses.
And that is the core of rebellion:
“God, I would follow You… if I were in charge.”
And it doesn’t end in elevation.
Numbers 16:31–33 says the ground split open and swallowed them alive.
Because God was making something clear:
You cannot grab what God has not given—without losing what He already entrusted.
Because this is where grace interrupts the story.
Moses told Aaron to take the censer and run into the camp.
And the Bible says he stood between the dead and the living—and the plague stopped (Numbers 16:48).
That moment is not just history.
Because one day, Jesus would stand between the dead and the living.
Romans 5:8 says, “God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
That includes the pride you never confessed.
The quiet thought that said, “I deserve more.”
You were not swallowed by judgment…
Because Christ was swallowed by death for you.
Religious people often reject authority… while claiming to honor God.
You are not called to compete.
You are not fighting for position.
You are being formed for purpose.
Stop trying to sit in a seat God never assigned…
When He is preparing you for something deeper than visibility.
That’s where real authority is born.
Because the same God who judged rebellion…
And He’s not asking you to earn your place.
He’s asking you to trust His grace.
Not hype. Just truth that stays with you when emotions fade.
And if God is stirring something in you right now…
Next post… we’re exposing the kind of obedience that actually unlocks authority.
Check the comments if you’re ready to go deeper.
